project.name: formcoach
project.description: Sensor-gated webcam form coaching: a wrist wearable (Seeed XIAO ESP32-S3 + BMI160) runs a tiny int8 neural network that detects exercise reps and gates a laptop pipeline using MediaPipe pose estimation and biomechanical rules to give per-rep form feedback on four dumbbell exercises.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Empty package marker for the formcoach.app module, which holds the live/replay pipeline, event logging, and overlay rendering.

nodes.name: events.py
nodes.summary: Defines the Event/EventLog data structures used to record pipeline lifecycle events and per-frame telemetry, and writes them to Parquet/JSON session artifacts.

nodes.name: Event
nodes.summary: Lightweight dataclass representing a single timestamped pipeline event (kind, time, payload) appended to an EventLog.

nodes.name: EventLog
nodes.summary: Accumulates Event records and per-frame telemetry during a session and writes them out as Parquet event/frame tables plus a JSON summary.

nodes.name: _json_default
nodes.summary: JSON serialization fallback that converts numpy arrays and scalars to native Python types for session summary output.

nodes.name: overlay.py
nodes.summary: OpenCV-based live overlay window that renders pose skeletons, rep counts, and form feedback on top of video frames during replay or live sessions.

nodes.name: Overlay
nodes.summary: Renders a live OpenCV window showing the pose skeleton, rep count, and latest fault feedback, updated on each pipeline event.

nodes.name: pipeline.py
nodes.summary: Core orchestration module that fuses IMU gating with MediaPipe pose landmarks to segment reps, compute per-rep biomechanical metrics, evaluate form rules, and drive both live and replay sessions.
nodes.languageNotes: Central integration point wiring together signal gating, pose estimation, rep segmentation and rule evaluation into a single event-emitting pipeline.

nodes.name: RepMetrics
nodes.summary: Dataclass capturing a single completed rep's timing, source (pose/IMU), angle traces, computed biomechanical metrics, and detected faults.

nodes.name: PipelineResult
nodes.summary: Aggregate result of a pipeline run: emitted events, frame counts, detected reps, and a summary dict, plus the output directory.

nodes.name: _UpEstimator
nodes.summary: Running estimator of the body's 'up' direction from shoulder/hip landmarks, used to disambiguate joint angle signs during live processing.

nodes.name: resample_rep_angles
nodes.summary: Resamples a rep's joint angle time series onto a fixed-length grid for consistent downstream metric computation.

nodes.name: metrics_from_angles
nodes.summary: Derives exercise-specific biomechanical metrics (ROM, tempo, symmetry, etc.) from resampled joint angle arrays for a single rep.

nodes.name: run_pipeline
nodes.summary: Main per-sample/per-frame loop that fuses IMU gating with pose frames, segments reps, computes metrics, evaluates rules, and emits lifecycle events; the heart of the live/replay pipeline.

nodes.name: _imu_reps
nodes.summary: Counts reps from IMU acceleration alone within gated segments, used as a fallback/cross-check against pose-based rep counting.

nodes.name: _fuse
nodes.summary: Merges pose-derived and IMU-derived rep counts into a single fused rep total for a session.

nodes.name: run_replay
nodes.summary: Entry point that loads a recorded replay session, wires up the gate, rules, event log and optional overlay, and drives run_pipeline in headless or windowed mode.

nodes.name: gating.py
nodes.summary: Runs replay sessions through the pipeline while measuring CPU/latency overhead of the IMU gate, and aggregates results into a Markdown benchmark report.

nodes.name: run_session
nodes.summary: Runs a single replay session through the pipeline while timing wall-clock and CPU usage to benchmark the IMU gate's overhead.

nodes.name: evaluate
nodes.summary: Evaluates gate performance across multiple sessions/gate configurations and writes a Markdown benchmark report with latency and CPU tables.

nodes.name: rules_eval.py
nodes.summary: Evaluation harness that replays MM-Fit pose sequences through the rep segmenter and rule engine to score rep-counting accuracy, rule pass rates under perturbation, and produce calibrated rule thresholds and figures.

nodes.name: _perturb
nodes.summary: Synthetically perturbs a rep's angle traces (e.g. amplitude scaling, timing shift) to test rule sensitivity to noisy input.

nodes.name: _reps_for_set
nodes.summary: Converts a raw MM-Fit pose set into segmented reps with resampled angle traces and computed metrics, ready for rule evaluation.

nodes.name: collect_reps
nodes.summary: Iterates MM-Fit workouts, extracts ground-truth labeled sets, and collects segmented reps across subjects into a single DataFrame.

nodes.name: evaluate
nodes.summary: Full rules evaluation pipeline: rep-count accuracy, rule pass rates, perturbation robustness, and metric distributions across exercises, written as a Markdown report with calibrated thresholds.

nodes.name: write_calibrated
nodes.summary: Writes a calibrated copy of the rules YAML document with thresholds adjusted from observed metric percentiles.

nodes.name: _fig_metrics
nodes.summary: Generates histogram figures of per-exercise metric distributions for the rules evaluation report.

nodes.name: replay.py
nodes.summary: Replay data sources that stream recorded IMU samples and pose sequences from disk at real or accelerated speed, standing in for live BLE/camera input during offline testing.

nodes.name: ReplaySource
nodes.summary: Replays recorded IMU samples from a Parquet session at real-time or accelerated speed, implementing the same interface as a live IMU source.

nodes.name: PoseFrame
nodes.summary: Dataclass representing a single replayed pose frame: timestamp, world landmarks, visibility, validity, and skeleton reference.

nodes.name: PoseReplay
nodes.summary: Iterable wrapper over a stored pose sequence that yields PoseFrame objects for a given session during replay.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package marker for the formcoach.pose module, which contains pose landmark extraction, normalization, angle computation, and rep segmentation.

nodes.name: angles.py
nodes.summary: Geometric utilities for computing joint and segment angles (degrees) from 3D pose landmarks, used to derive exercise-specific biomechanical metrics.

nodes.name: joint_angles
nodes.summary: Computes the full set of joint angles (elbow, shoulder, knee, etc.) needed for rule evaluation from a single frame or sequence of 3D pose landmarks.

nodes.name: landmarker.py
nodes.summary: Wraps MediaPipe's PoseLandmarker to extract 3D pose landmarks from recorded video and writes results to the pose Parquet store, used for offline dataset preparation.
nodes.languageNotes: Lazily imports MediaPipe and OpenCV so the module stays importable without the optional 'vision' extra installed.

nodes.name: FrameResult
nodes.summary: Dataclass holding a single extracted video frame's timestamp, image-space and world-space pose landmarks.

nodes.name: make_landmarker
nodes.summary: Constructs a MediaPipe PoseLandmarker configured for video mode from a bundled model asset.

nodes.name: open_video
nodes.summary: Opens a video file with OpenCV and yields frames with their timestamps for pose extraction.

nodes.name: extract_frames
nodes.summary: Runs pose detection over a stream of frames, returning a FrameResult for each detected frame.

nodes.name: results_to_parquet
nodes.summary: Converts a list of FrameResults into image/world landmark arrays and writes them to the pose Parquet store.

nodes.name: extract_video
nodes.summary: End-to-end entry point that extracts pose landmarks from a video file and caches the result to Parquet, skipping work if already extracted.

nodes.name: normalize.py
nodes.summary: Normalizes raw pose landmark sequences (up-vector estimation, gap-filling, scale normalization) and smooths derived joint angle traces before rule evaluation.

nodes.name: estimate_up_vector
nodes.summary: Estimates the body's vertical 'up' direction from shoulder and hip landmarks, used to orient joint angle calculations consistently.

nodes.name: _fill_gaps
nodes.summary: Linearly interpolates short gaps of missing/low-confidence landmark data up to a maximum gap length.

nodes.name: normalize_sequence
nodes.summary: Validates, gap-fills, and scale-normalizes a pose landmark sequence using torso length, preparing it for angle computation.

nodes.name: smooth_angles
nodes.summary: Smooths a joint angle time series with median filtering and Savitzky-Golay smoothing after interpolating NaN gaps.

nodes.name: reps.py
nodes.summary: Segments a continuous joint-angle signal into individual exercise repetitions using hysteresis thresholds with optional adaptive calibration.

nodes.name: PoseRep
nodes.summary: Dataclass describing a single segmented repetition: start/end/extreme times, indices, extreme angle value, and duration.

nodes.name: RepSegmenter
nodes.summary: Stateful hysteresis-based segmenter that detects repetition boundaries from a streaming joint-angle signal, with optional adaptive threshold calibration from recent history.

nodes.name: segment_reps
nodes.summary: Batch convenience wrapper that runs RepSegmenter over a full angle/time series and returns all detected PoseRep segments.

nodes.name: skeletons.py
nodes.summary: Defines the Skeleton joint-naming schema and a helper to look up a named joint's 3D coordinates across pose/landmark arrays.

nodes.name: Skeleton
nodes.summary: Named joint schema with alias resolution, used to look up joint indices consistently across MM-Fit and MediaPipe skeleton layouts.

nodes.name: joint
nodes.summary: Looks up a named joint's 3D coordinates from a landmark array using a Skeleton's joint index/alias mapping.

nodes.name: store.py
nodes.summary: Reads and writes pose landmark sequences to/from Parquet, flattening per-joint world/image coordinates into wide columns for efficient storage.

nodes.name: PoseSequence
nodes.summary: Dataclass bundling a session's pose landmark sequence: world/image coordinates, timestamps, skeleton, validity, and visibility.

nodes.name: write_pose
nodes.summary: Flattens per-joint world/image landmark arrays into wide columns and writes a pose sequence to a Parquet file.

nodes.name: read_pose
nodes.summary: Reads a Parquet pose file back into a PoseSequence, reconstructing the per-joint world/image landmark arrays.

nodes.name: engine.py
nodes.summary: Loads exercise form rules from YAML and evaluates computed rep metrics against per-exercise thresholds to produce Fault objects for coaching feedback.

nodes.name: Condition
nodes.summary: Dataclass representing a single threshold condition (metric, comparison operator, threshold value) within a rule.

nodes.name: Rule
nodes.summary: Dataclass representing a named form-check rule: severity, feedback message, and the metric conditions that trigger it.

nodes.name: Fault
nodes.summary: Represents a triggered rule violation for a rep, carrying the offending metric, value, threshold, and human-readable feedback message.

nodes.name: RuleEngine
nodes.summary: Loads exercise rule definitions from YAML and evaluates a rep's metrics against each exercise's rule set, producing Fault objects and exposing rep-segmentation config per exercise.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package root for the formcoach library; re-exports selected top-level symbols (e.g. SessionRecorder) used by the CLI and other modules.

nodes.name: cli.py
nodes.summary: Typer-based `formcoach` CLI entry point exposing data, feature, training, evaluation, demo and recording subcommands that delegate to the library's data/signal/eval/models packages, per ADR-0008 (every Makefile target goes through this CLI).
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Typer Option/Argument decorators plus small Enum classes (Dataset, Source, Gate, Task) to constrain CLI choices; many subcommands are still stubs that print a not-implemented message.

nodes.name: stub
nodes.summary: Prints a standardized 'not yet implemented' message for CLI subcommands that are still placeholders.

nodes.name: _version
nodes.summary: Typer callback that prints the formcoach package version and exits when --version is passed.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Root Typer callback registered for the top-level `formcoach` command group, wiring in the --version option.

nodes.name: data_fetch
nodes.summary: `formcoach data fetch` subcommand that downloads/verifies a public dataset (MM-Fit, RecoFit, RecGym) against data/MANIFEST.md, optionally including team video.

nodes.name: data_convert
nodes.summary: `formcoach data convert` subcommand that converts a raw dataset into standardized Parquet IMU/pose streams via the data.convert module.

nodes.name: data_profile
nodes.summary: `formcoach data profile` subcommand that writes a dataset profiling report (minutes per subject/exercise, sample figures) via data.profile.

nodes.name: data_make_fixtures
nodes.summary: `formcoach data make-fixtures` subcommand that builds the small committed test fixtures under data/fixtures/.

nodes.name: features_build
nodes.summary: `formcoach features build` subcommand that windows and featurizes IMU streams for a dataset via signal.build.build_features.

nodes.name: pose_extract
nodes.summary: `formcoach pose extract` subcommand that runs the MediaPipe pose landmarker over a video file to produce a pose Parquet stream.

nodes.name: train_gate
nodes.summary: `formcoach train gate` subcommand that trains the IMU gate model (random forest or CNN, with optional int8 export) via models.train.

nodes.name: eval_all
nodes.summary: `formcoach eval all` subcommand that runs the full evaluation suite (LOSO, repcount, rules, gating, etc.) as a sequence of CLI subprocess calls, optionally in quick mode.

nodes.name: eval_loso
nodes.summary: `formcoach eval loso` subcommand that runs leave-one-subject-out evaluation of the gate model and writes a headline report, delegating to eval.loso_cli.run.

nodes.name: eval_repcount
nodes.summary: `formcoach eval repcount` subcommand that evaluates rep-counting accuracy on recorded/replay sessions via eval.repcount.evaluate.

nodes.name: eval_rules
nodes.summary: `formcoach eval rules` subcommand that evaluates form-feedback rule accuracy and can write a calibrated rules.yaml via eval.rules_eval.evaluate.

nodes.name: eval_gating
nodes.summary: `formcoach eval gating` subcommand that evaluates the IMU-to-pose gate decision on recorded team sessions via eval.gating.evaluate.

nodes.name: eval_device
nodes.summary: `formcoach eval device` subcommand that parses a device firmware log and writes a latency/memory benchmark report via eval.device.evaluate.

nodes.name: demo
nodes.summary: `formcoach demo` subcommand that runs the end-to-end form-coaching pipeline (replay, serial, or BLE source) headless or with an overlay window, applying the rule engine to produce feedback.

nodes.name: _open_source
nodes.summary: Opens the appropriate IMU/pose data source (fake replay, serial, or BLE) for the demo/record commands based on the --source option.

nodes.name: record
nodes.summary: `formcoach record` subcommand that captures a live wearable/camera session to data/team/ via SessionRecorder, enforcing the team-recording protocol (S1-S5 subjects, no pushed video).

nodes.name: session_check
nodes.summary: `formcoach session check` subcommand that validates a recorded session directory and prints a status report via SessionChecker.

nodes.name: Dataset
nodes.summary: Enum of supported dataset choices (mmfit, recofit, recgym, team) used to constrain CLI --dataset options.

nodes.name: Source
nodes.summary: Enum of supported input source choices (replay, serial, ble) used to constrain CLI --source options for demo/record commands.

nodes.name: Gate
nodes.summary: Enum of gate model backends (e.g. rf, cnn) used to constrain the CLI --gate/--model options.

nodes.name: Task
nodes.summary: Enum of LOSO evaluation task choices (e.g. active detection vs. exercise classification) used by the eval loso subcommand.

nodes.name: convert.py
nodes.summary: Converts raw per-dataset loader output (MM-Fit, RecoFit, RecGym, team) into standardized, schema-validated IMU/pose Parquet stream files under data/processed/.

nodes.name: convert_dataset
nodes.summary: Loads a raw dataset via the registered per-dataset loader and writes each workout/visit/session stream as a validated Parquet file, returning the list of written paths.

nodes.name: list_streams
nodes.summary: Lists already-converted stream files for one or all datasets under the processed data root, parsing subject/session/device from filenames.

nodes.name: StreamFile
nodes.summary: Dataclass describing a converted stream file's dataset, subject, session, device and path, returned by list_streams.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package init for the formcoach.eval evaluation suite (LOSO, repcount, rules, gating, device, report modules).

nodes.name: device.py
nodes.summary: Parses ESP32-S3 firmware serial log output (inference latency, arena/flash usage, per-class counts) and writes a device benchmark Markdown report.

nodes.name: parse
nodes.summary: Parses firmware log text with regexes to extract inference latency (us), flash/RAM usage, and per-class prediction counts.

nodes.name: evaluate
nodes.summary: Reads a device log file, computes latency percentiles and memory footprint statistics, and writes a headline device-benchmark Markdown report.

nodes.name: loso.py
nodes.summary: Core leave-one-subject-out (LOSO) and group-k-fold evaluation harness: split generation, feature extraction helpers, fold execution, metric aggregation, confusion-matrix figures and Markdown report writing.
nodes.languageNotes: Headline metrics must be leave-one-subject-out per CLAUDE.md working rule #8; this module is the shared implementation used by both the CLI and loso_cli.run.

nodes.name: loso_splits
nodes.summary: Builds leave-one-subject-out train/test index splits from a group (subject id) array.

nodes.name: group_kfold_splits
nodes.summary: Builds randomized, group-aware k-fold train/test index splits (subjects never split across folds) for faster evaluation than full LOSO.

nodes.name: check_units
nodes.summary: Validates that a windowed features DataFrame uses a single, consistent unit system (e.g. SI), raising ValueError otherwise.

nodes.name: energy_features
nodes.summary: Computes a simple acceleration-magnitude-variance baseline feature from raw IMU windows, used as the energy-baseline model input.

nodes.name: run_loso
nodes.summary: Runs the full LOSO (or group-k-fold) loop: fits a fresh model per fold via make_model, predicts on the held-out subject, and aggregates per-fold and pooled accuracy/F1/confusion metrics into a LosoResult.

nodes.name: result_from_predictions
nodes.summary: Builds a LosoResult (per-fold and pooled metrics, confusion matrix) directly from precomputed out-of-fold predictions, used when predictions come from an external caller (e.g. the CLI CNN path).

nodes.name: _fig_confusion
nodes.summary: Renders a normalized confusion-matrix heatmap figure (matplotlib) for a LosoResult and saves it as a PNG under reports/.

nodes.name: write_loso_report
nodes.summary: Writes a headline LOSO evaluation Markdown report (summary stats, per-fold table, confusion-matrix figure) to reports/, regenerated by `make eval` rather than hand-edited.

nodes.name: LosoResult
nodes.summary: Dataclass holding LOSO evaluation outputs: per-fold metrics table, pooled metrics dict, confusion matrix, labels, and raw predictions/groups.

nodes.name: loso_cli.py
nodes.summary: CLI-facing orchestration for the `formcoach eval loso` command: loads windowed features, builds X/y, selects an RF or CNN model factory, runs LOSO or a held-out-test evaluation, and writes the report.

nodes.name: _xy
nodes.summary: Builds the (X, y) feature matrix and label vector for a given task (active-detection or exercise-classification) from a windowed-features DataFrame, choosing energy or full feature sets by model type.

nodes.name: _factory
nodes.summary: Returns a per-fold model-construction closure (make_rf or a CNN LOSO factory) parameterized by model name, task, epoch count and optional int8 export store.

nodes.name: _load
nodes.summary: Loads windowed features for a dataset, validates unit consistency, and filters to only active (in-exercise) windows.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Top-level LOSO evaluation runner invoked by `formcoach eval loso`: loads data, builds features, runs LOSO (or trains once and evaluates on a held-out test dataset for a transfer check), and writes the headline report.

nodes.name: report.py
nodes.summary: Shared Markdown report-writing helpers (git-commit header, formatted tables, relative figure paths) used by every evaluation module under formcoach.eval.

nodes.name: git_commit
nodes.summary: Returns the current short git commit hash (or a fallback) for stamping reproducibility metadata into generated reports.

nodes.name: header
nodes.summary: Builds a standardized Markdown report header (title, timestamp, git commit, command, seed, and extra key/value metadata lines) shared by all eval reports.

nodes.name: md_table
nodes.summary: Renders a pandas DataFrame as a GitHub-flavored Markdown table with configurable float formatting.

nodes.name: relative_figure
nodes.summary: Computes a figure file's path relative to its report's directory, for embedding as a portable Markdown image link.

nodes.name: rf.py
nodes.summary: Factory for the scikit-learn RandomForestClassifier used as the baseline IMU gate model.

nodes.name: make_rf
nodes.summary: Constructs a seeded RandomForestClassifier with configurable estimator count and parallelism, used as the gate model's RF backend in both training and LOSO evaluation.

nodes.name: train.py
nodes.summary: Trains the IMU gate model — either a scikit-learn random forest (train_rf_gate) or a Keras 1D-CNN with optional int8 TFLite export (train_cnn_gate) — from windowed feature data, writing a headline training report.
nodes.languageNotes: train_cnn_gate produces both a float and int8-quantized TFLite model plus a C header/source pair for TensorFlow Lite Micro on the ESP32-S3, matching the device.export pipeline used by firmware.

nodes.name: train_rf_gate
nodes.summary: Loads windowed features across one or more datasets, fits a random-forest gate model (active-detection or exercise classification) via make_rf, and saves the model plus training metadata to disk.

nodes.name: train_cnn_gate
nodes.summary: Trains a Keras 1D-CNN gate model on windowed IMU data, evaluates float vs. int8-quantized accuracy/F1, optionally exports int8 TFLite plus a C header for TFLite Micro, and writes a training report.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package init for formcoach.signal, the IMU-only signal processing pipeline (resample, filters, windowing, features, rep counting); kept free of formcoach.pose imports per the IMU-only fallback rule.

nodes.name: build.py
nodes.summary: Builds windowed IMU feature Parquet files from converted streams (optionally in parallel via ProcessPoolExecutor) and loads them back for training/evaluation.

nodes.name: _build_one
nodes.summary: Worker function (used by a process pool) that reads one IMU stream Parquet file, windows and featurizes it, and writes the resulting windowed-features Parquet file.

nodes.name: build_features
nodes.summary: Discovers all converted streams for a dataset, skips already-built outputs unless forced, and dispatches _build_one across a process pool to produce windowed feature files.

nodes.name: load_windows
nodes.summary: Loads and concatenates all windowed-feature Parquet files for a dataset, optionally filtering by minimum window purity and device set.

nodes.name: features.py
nodes.summary: Per-channel and per-window statistical/spectral feature extraction (mean, std, RMS, dominant frequency, spectral entropy, autocorrelation-based periodicity, min/max) for IMU windows.

nodes.name: _channel_stats
nodes.summary: Computes a fixed set of time- and frequency-domain statistics (mean, std, RMS, dominant frequency, spectral entropy, periodicity via autocorrelation, min, max) for a single 1D channel signal.

nodes.name: window_features
nodes.summary: Computes per-axis and acceleration-magnitude channel statistics for a single IMU window, returning a named feature dict.

nodes.name: featurize_windows
nodes.summary: Applies window_features across all windows in a DataFrame, attaching the resulting feature columns back onto the window metadata.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package init for the data loaders subpackage; exposes a `loader(name)` dispatcher that lazily imports the MM-Fit, RecoFit, or RecGym dataset loader module by name.

nodes.name: loader
nodes.summary: Resolves a dataset name (mmfit/recofit/recgym) to its loader module via dynamic import, raising a clear error for unknown datasets.

nodes.name: labels.py
nodes.summary: Defines the canonical exercise-label vocabulary and a `canonical()` mapping function that normalizes raw per-dataset exercise labels (MM-Fit, RecoFit, RecGym) into FormCoach's four frozen exercise classes plus idle/other.

nodes.name: canonical
nodes.summary: Maps a dataset-specific raw exercise label string to FormCoach's canonical label set, used by every dataset loader to unify labels.

nodes.name: mmfit.py
nodes.summary: Loader for the MM-Fit public dataset: discovers workouts, aligns IMU/pose modalities via a fitted session clock, loads per-set labels, and builds canonical IMU streams and 3D pose sequences.

nodes.name: load_modality
nodes.summary: Loads a single MM-Fit sensor modality .npy file for a workout, tolerating minor filename variants.

nodes.name: load_labels
nodes.summary: Parses an MM-Fit workout's per-set labels CSV (start/end frame, reps, exercise) into a DataFrame.

nodes.name: SessionClock
nodes.summary: Small linear-fit clock mapping MM-Fit frame indices and device millisecond timestamps to a common seconds timeline for cross-modality alignment.

nodes.name: session_clock
nodes.summary: Fits a SessionClock for a workout by linearly regressing pose-frame indices against device pose timestamps.

nodes.name: _merge_acc_gyr
nodes.summary: Merges separate accelerometer and gyroscope arrays onto a common deduplicated timestamp grid via interpolation.

nodes.name: load_stream
nodes.summary: Builds a canonical IMU stream DataFrame for one MM-Fit workout/device by loading raw sensor data, aligning it to the session clock, attaching per-sample rep/set/exercise labels, and validating units via the shared schema.

nodes.name: load_sets
nodes.summary: Loads a workout's labeled sets table and augments it with subject id and clock-converted start/end times in seconds.

nodes.name: load_pose3d
nodes.summary: Loads the 3D pose ground-truth modality for a workout and reshapes it to (joint, axis, frame) with clock-aligned timestamps.

nodes.name: iter_streams
nodes.summary: Generator yielding (workout, device, IMU stream) tuples across all discovered MM-Fit workouts for one or more devices.

nodes.name: describe
nodes.summary: Computes summary statistics for the MM-Fit dataset (workout/set/rep counts, per-device sample rates and dropped-sample counts) used to build the data profiling report.

nodes.name: profile.py
nodes.summary: Generates a Markdown dataset-profile report summarizing all available public datasets (MM-Fit, RecoFit, RecGym) with per-exercise minutes tables and example figures, used to check data hygiene before modeling.

nodes.name: _minutes_table
nodes.summary: Builds a combined DataFrame of minutes-of-data-per-exercise-per-dataset by calling each available loader's describe() output and merging the results.

nodes.name: _fig_minutes
nodes.summary: Renders and saves a grouped bar chart of minutes of data per exercise per dataset.

nodes.name: _fig_mmfit_example
nodes.summary: Plots an example MM-Fit IMU trace with labeled set spans overlaid, saved as a figure for the profile report.

nodes.name: _mmfit_section
nodes.summary: Builds the Markdown section describing MM-Fit dataset coverage (per-device rates, missing modalities, dropped-sample rates).

nodes.name: _recofit_section
nodes.summary: Builds the Markdown section describing RecoFit dataset coverage and signal ranges.

nodes.name: _recgym_section
nodes.summary: Builds the Markdown section describing RecGym dataset coverage (subjects, positions, sessions).

nodes.name: write_profile
nodes.summary: Top-level entry that assembles the full dataset profile Markdown report (headers, per-dataset sections, minutes table, figures) and writes it to disk; invoked by `formcoach data profile`.

nodes.name: default_roots
nodes.summary: Returns the default external-data root paths for each dataset the profile report scans.

nodes.name: recgym.py
nodes.summary: Loader for the RecGym public dataset (single CSV of subject/position/session IMU recordings); builds canonical IMU streams per subject-position-session and computes dataset summary statistics.

nodes.name: load_stream
nodes.summary: Loads one RecGym subject/position/session block from the master CSV, derives contiguous rep/set ids from exercise-label run changes, and builds a canonical IMU stream.

nodes.name: describe
nodes.summary: Computes RecGym dataset summary statistics: minutes per workout, subject/session counts, positions, and signal value ranges.

nodes.name: recofit.py
nodes.summary: Loader for the RecoFit public dataset distributed as MATLAB .mat files; parses nested MATLAB struct arrays into per-subject-visit segment tables and canonical IMU streams.

nodes.name: _segments_of
nodes.summary: Extracts the labeled activity-segment table (start/end time, canonical label) from a parsed RecoFit MATLAB subject record.

nodes.name: load_stream
nodes.summary: Builds a canonical IMU stream for a RecoFit subject/visit by aligning accelerometer and gyroscope channels onto a shared timeline and attaching per-sample segment labels.

nodes.name: describe
nodes.summary: Computes RecoFit dataset summary statistics: subject count, sample rates, minutes per exercise, and single-participant activity metadata.

nodes.name: schema.py
nodes.summary: Defines FormCoach's canonical IMU stream Parquet schema (§5 of the system design doc) plus constructor and strict validator functions used by every dataset loader and the live session recorder.
nodes.languageNotes: Central contract enforcing units (m/s^2, rad/s, seconds) and column layout shared by all data producers and consumers.

nodes.name: SchemaError
nodes.summary: Exception type raised when a DataFrame fails IMU stream schema validation.

nodes.name: is_active
nodes.summary: Returns whether a canonical exercise label counts as an active repetition (excludes idle/other), used by windowing and rep-counting code.

nodes.name: empty_imu_stream
nodes.summary: Builds a zero-length IMU stream DataFrame with the correct schema, useful as a placeholder or for testing.

nodes.name: make_imu_stream
nodes.summary: Canonical constructor that assembles a fully-typed IMU stream DataFrame from raw timestamp, accelerometer, and gyroscope arrays plus dataset/subject/label metadata; used by every dataset loader and the recorder.

nodes.name: validate_imu_stream
nodes.summary: Strictly validates an IMU stream DataFrame against the schema contract: required columns, dtypes, monotonic time, finite values, allowed label/placement/unit sets, and plausible accelerometer/gyroscope magnitude ranges.

nodes.name: repcount.py
nodes.summary: Evaluation harness that runs the IMU rep-counting algorithm against MM-Fit ground-truth set/rep counts, aggregates per-exercise error statistics, and writes a Markdown report with an error boxplot.

nodes.name: count_sets

nodes.name: gate.h

nodes.summary: Empty package marker for the `formcoach.io` package containing the BLE, serial, and protocol I/O modules.

nodes.name: protocol.py

nodes.summary: Debounces boolean gate decisions by requiring N consecutive on/off votes before flipping state, preventing rapid gate flapping.

nodes.name: GateBase
nodes.summary: Abstract base class defining the gate interface (`update`) that all gating strategies implement.

nodes.name: AlwaysOnGate

nodes.summary: Windowed gate strategy that loads a trained scikit-learn/joblib classifier and runs it on extracted window features to decide activation on the laptop.

nodes.name: make_gate
nodes.summary: Factory function that constructs the configured gate strategy (`always_on`, `energy`, `laptop`, `device`) by name.

nodes.name: _bleak
nodes.summary: Lazily imports the optional `bleak` BLE library, raising a clear install hint if the device extra is missing.

nodes.summary: Packs a `Status` record into its fixed-size binary wire representation.

nodes.name: unpack_status
nodes.summary: Validates and decodes a fixed-size binary buffer into a `Status` record.

nodes.summary: Parses a comma-delimited ASCII telemetry line from the serial fallback path into a `Sample`.

nodes.summary: Lazily imports the optional `pyserial` dependency, raising a clear install hint if missing.

nodes.summary: Lists available serial ports (e.g. `/dev/ttyACM0`, `COMx`) for interactive device selection.

nodes.summary: USB-serial `IMUSource` implementation that opens a serial port, sends start/stop commands, and yields decoded `SISample` objects with drop tracking.

nodes.name: SISample
nodes.summary: SI-unit IMU sample (acceleration in m/s², angular rate in rad/s, gate/session flags, arrival timestamp) shared by all data sources and consumed by the pipeline and rep-detection code.

nodes.summary: Abstract iterator interface (`iter_samples`, `close`) implemented by the BLE, serial, and fake IMU data sources.

nodes.name: from_raw
nodes.summary: Converts a raw protocol `Sample` into an SI-unit `SISample`, recording the laptop-side arrival timestamp.

nodes.name: filters.py

nodes.name: lowpass
nodes.summary: Applies a zero-phase Butterworth low-pass filter to a signal at a given sample rate and cutoff frequency.

nodes.name: highpass
nodes.summary: Applies a zero-phase Butterworth high-pass filter to a signal at a given sample rate and cutoff frequency.

nodes.name: bandpass
nodes.summary: Applies a zero-phase Butterworth band-pass filter between a low and high cutoff frequency, used to isolate the repetition-motion frequency band of IMU data.

nodes.name: gravity.py
nodes.summary: Separates the gravity component from accelerometer readings via low-pass filtering and computes signal magnitude, supporting downstream rep detection and feature extraction on the IMU signal.

nodes.name: split_gravity
nodes.summary: Splits a 3-axis accelerometer signal into a gravity component (via low-pass filtering) and returns it for subtraction to recover linear acceleration.

nodes.name: magnitude
nodes.summary: Computes the per-sample Euclidean norm (magnitude) of a 3-axis accelerometer signal.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: FormCoach pairs a wrist wearable (Seeed XIAO ESP32-S3 + BMI160 IMU) with a laptop webcam pipeline: the wearable's on-device CNN detects when an exercise rep is happening and gates a MediaPipe pose pipeline on the laptop, which applies biomechanical rules to give per-rep form feedback on four dumbbell exercises (curl, press, lateral raise, squat). README.md gives the 5-minute quickstart and everyday `make` commands every step of this tour will reference. Keep this mental model going forward: sensor gate -> pose -> rules -> feedback, built to work end-to-end on public datasets even before any hardware exists.

tour.title: Build Order and Working Rules
tour.description: docs/00-START-HERE.md lays out the seven checkpoints the team builds through, and CLAUDE.md codifies the non-negotiable rules that shape every file you'll see: public-data-first (hardware never blocks software), small reviewable PRs, reproducibility via `uv`/`make`, and a strict import boundary keeping `formcoach.signal` free of `formcoach.pose` so the IMU-only fallback always builds. These constraints explain design choices you'll notice throughout the codebase, like why almost every pipeline stage has a `--source replay` path.

tour.title: The CLI Entry Point
tour.description: src/formcoach/cli.py is the single Typer entry point for the whole project (`formcoach ...`); every Makefile target delegates to a subcommand here (data fetch/convert/profile, features build, train-gate, eval *, demo, record, session-check). With the highest fan-out of any Python file, it is the map of the entire pipeline: read its subcommands top to bottom and you see the exact data -> signal -> models -> app -> eval flow the rest of this tour walks through in depth.
tour.languageLesson: Typer builds a CLI from type-annotated function signatures and docstrings, so each subcommand here is just a plain Python function decorated with `@app.command()` — no manual argparse wiring.

tour.title: Data Layer: Schema and Loaders
tour.description: Everything downstream depends on a single canonical IMU stream schema. file:src/formcoach/data/schema.py defines that Parquet schema (§5 of the system design doc) and is the most depended-upon file in the codebase (13 incoming references), while data/__init__.py's loader() dispatcher lazily imports per-dataset loaders for MM-Fit, RecoFit, and RecGym so heavy dependencies stay optional. fetch.py handles downloading/verifying/extracting those public datasets, and convert.py normalizes each loader's raw output into the shared schema — this is the 'public data first' rule from Step 2 made concrete.

tour.title: Data Manifest and Fixtures
tour.description: data/MANIFEST.md is the ledger that data/manifest.py reads and updates: every external dataset file gets a URL, SHA-256 hash, size, and license recorded here, enforcing the data-hygiene rule that raw/processed data stays gitignored while only small fixtures get committed. data/fixtures.py synthesizes tiny deterministic stand-ins for MM-Fit/RecoFit/RecGym so tests and CI never need the real (large, licensed) datasets — this is what lets `make test` run on a fresh clone with no downloads.

tour.title: IMU Signal Processing (Hardware-Free Path)
tour.description: The signal/ package is the pure IMU-only pipeline that never imports from pose — this boundary is enforced so the on-device gate and its fallback can ship even if the vision stack breaks. windows.py slices a canonical stream into fixed-length overlapping windows with majority-vote labels; features.py extracts per-window statistical/spectral features; filters.py and gravity.py provide the Butterworth filtering and gravity-separation these build on; and reps.py detects individual repetitions directly from acceleration, the same detection logic later mirrored on the firmware.
tour.languageLesson: SciPy's second-order-section (sosfiltfilt) Butterworth filters are used instead of naive difference-equation filters because SOS form is numerically stable at the filter orders needed for real-time IMU denoising.

tour.title: Gate Models: Deciding 'Rep in Progress'
tour.description: Building on the windowed features from Step 6, models/ trains the classifier that decides whether an exercise rep is currently happening — the 'gate' that wakes up the expensive pose pipeline. models/cnn.py defines and trains the 1D-CNN that becomes the on-device model, models/rf.py and models/energy.py provide simpler random-forest and energy-threshold baselines for comparison, and models/export.py converts the trained Keras CNN to a quantized int8 TFLite model small enough to run on the ESP32-S3's TensorFlow Lite Micro runtime.

tour.title: IO: BLE, Serial, and Replay Sources
tour.description: The io/ package defines how IMU samples reach the laptop, all behind one shared interface. source.py's abstract IMUSource and SISample model let the rest of the app treat live BLE (ble.py), USB-serial fallback (serial_source.py), and recorded replay (replay.py) interchangeably — this is what makes `formcoach demo --source replay --headless` always work even with zero hardware attached. protocol.py is the Python mirror of the firmware's wire protocol (Step 11), so BLE/serial decoding here must always match protocol.h exactly.

tour.title: Pose Extraction and Biomechanics
tour.description: Once the gate says a rep is happening, the pose/ package takes over: landmarker.py wraps MediaPipe's PoseLandmarker to extract 3D joint positions from video, normalize.py corrects for camera angle and scale, angles.py computes the joint angles (elbow flexion, torso lean, etc.) that biomechanical rules depend on, and pose/reps.py segments a continuous joint-angle signal into individual reps using hysteresis thresholds — the vision-side counterpart to signal/reps.py from Step 6.

tour.title: Application Pipeline and Rules Engine
tour.description: app/pipeline.py is where everything from Steps 6-9 fuses together: it uses the gate (app/gate.py, which wraps always-on/energy/device/laptop-ML strategies) to decide when to run pose extraction, segments reps, computes per-rep metrics, and hands them to the rules engine. rules/engine.py loads per-exercise thresholds from rules.yaml (the default calibration) and evaluates each rep's metrics against them to produce pass/fail feedback — the final output a user sees for each of the four exercises.

tour.title: Firmware: On-Device Gate
tour.description: firmware/src/app/main.cpp is the Arduino-style entry point running on the wearable itself — it wires up BLE advertising, the BMI160 IMU driver, the on-device Gate, and status UI. gate.cpp loads the same int8 TFLite model exported in Step 7 and runs it through TensorFlow Lite Micro to make the identical 'rep in progress' decision the Python-side energy/CNN gates make, but directly on the ESP32-S3. protocol.h is the C-side source of truth for the wire format that io/protocol.py (Step 8) mirrors exactly — the two files change together, pinned by tests/test_protocol.py.
tour.languageLesson: TensorFlow Lite Micro runs a pre-compiled, statically-allocated interpreter with no dynamic memory allocation or filesystem access, which is why the quantized model is embedded directly as a C byte array (gate_model_data.cc) rather than loaded from a file.

tour.title: Evaluation as a First-Class Deliverable
tour.description: eval/loso.py implements leave-one-subject-out cross-validation, the headline evaluation method the project insists on — never seen-subject accuracy — so gate models are judged on genuinely unseen subjects. eval/rules_eval.py replays MM-Fit pose sequences through the rep segmenter and rules engine from Step 10 to validate the rules against ground truth, eval/gating.py benchmarks always-on vs. energy vs. laptop gating strategies, and eval/report.py writes the shared Markdown table/figure helpers every report in reports/ is generated from, never hand-edited.

tour.title: Generated Reports
tour.description: reports/loso_cnn-int8_active_recofit.md and reports/gating.md are concrete outputs of the eval/ harness from Step 12 — auto-generated, never hand-edited, and regenerated by `make eval`. They show how the int8-quantized on-device CNN gate (Step 11's firmware target) compares to the float CNN and simpler baselines on unseen subjects, and how the three gating strategies trade off CPU/latency overhead, turning the abstract 'evaluation is first-class' rule from Step 2 into numbers the team can cite in the final report.

tour.title: Tests and CI
tour.description: tests/test_protocol.py pins the BLE/serial packet contract on both the Python and firmware sides so protocol.py and protocol.h (Step 11) can never silently drift apart, and tests/test_replay_pipeline.py is the integration test that runs the full replay pipeline end-to-end on a 30-second fixture. .github/workflows/ci.yml runs this suite plus ruff lint and a firmware `pio run` build on every push and PR, while the Makefile is the single orchestrator (`make setup lint test data features train-gate eval demo record fw-build`) that both CI and every teammate use to invoke these same steps locally.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions workflows define parallel `jobs` (here: lint, test, firmware) each running independent `steps`; caching the uv and PlatformIO toolchains between runs is what keeps CI fast despite installing a full embedded toolchain on every PR.

tour.title: Decisions, Status, and Handoff Docs
tour.description: docs/DECISIONS.md is the ADR log recording why the team chose `uv` over pip, Typer over argparse, TFLite Micro over alternatives, and every other fork in the road referenced implicitly throughout this tour; docs/STATUS.md is the running session log that always starts a work session (most recent entry first: what changed, what's next, open questions, blockers). docs/howto/cnn-gate.md and docs/howto/replay-demo.md are teammate-facing handoff guides for the gate-training workflow (Step 7) and the hardware-free replay demo (Step 8) — the pattern every completed task in this repo is written up in so a less-experienced teammate can take it over without debugging toolchains.
